name: Muscat
tagline: Serene Arabian coast of forts, wadis and white minarets.
bestMonths: Jan, Feb, Mar, Apr, Nov and Dec
whenBlurb: Come October to March, mild and pleasant, and time it to the January Muscat Festival; for the green Khareef monsoon head south to Salalah July-August, and avoid Muscat's May-to-September heat.

ourTake.lede: Muscat is the antidote to the Gulf's glass towers, low white buildings, a real corniche, and mountains that fall straight into the sea. Don't treat it as a one-night stop; base here and drive out to the wadis and Nizwa. Skip the beach-resort bubble and spend a night in the Hajar mountains instead.
ourTake.comeIf: You want Arabia with its dignity intact - forts, wadis and empty coast rather than glass towers.
ourTake.skipIf: You want nightlife, big shopping and constant motion; Oman is deliberately gentle.

guide.lede: Where to stay, what to do, where to eat, and where the night goes, grouped by price, every address earned by a name worth trusting.

items.name: The Chedi Muscat
items.area: Al Ghubra North, Shatti Al Qurum
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards, #4 Hotel in the Middle East (2025); #1 Hotel in the Middle East (2024)
World Travel Awards, World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa (2022, 2023, 2024, 2025)
items.description: GHM's serene, minimalist beachfront sanctuary, the hotel that defined understated luxury in the Gulf, and Oman's one true icon.

items.name: Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
items.area: Al Bustan, between the Hajar mountains and the sea
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide Recommended (2025)
World Travel Awards, World's Leading Palace Hotel (2018)
Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice, Top-5 Hotel in the Middle East (2018)
items.description: A former royal-guest palace turned seaside grand hotel, a soaring 38-metre atrium, private beach and mountains at its back.

items.name: Mandarin Oriental, Muscat
credentials: Mandarin Oriental Hotel Group (Leading maison group; Forbes Travel Guide inspected, 'soon to be rated')
Opened June 2024, the brand's first hotel in Oman
items.description: The group's Oman debut, a bright-white beachfront house where Omani craft meets Mandarin Oriental's quiet precision.

items.name: Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar Resort
items.area: Jebal Akhdar (Green Mountain), ~2hr drive from Muscat
credentials: Condé Nast Traveler Gold List (2020)
World Travel Awards, Oman's Leading Luxury Resort (2020, 2021, 2022)
items.description: One of the highest resorts on earth, perched 2,000m on a canyon rim where Princess Diana once stood, a genuine mountain escape.

items.name: Al Husn, a Waldorf Astoria Hotel
credentials: Waldorf Astoria Hotels & Resorts, Oman debut of the brand (rebranded from Shangri-La Al Husn, 1 Jan 2026; Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star as Shangri-La Al Husn)
Part of the landmark Barr Al Jissah resort complex
items.description: An adults-oriented clifftop 'castle' above a private turquoise cove, the crown of the Barr Al Jissah headland, now under the Waldorf Astoria flag.

items.name: Alila Jabal Akhdar
items.area: Jebal Akhdar (Green Mountain), ~2hr drive from Muscat
credentials: World Travel Awards, Oman's Leading Resort (2023, 2024); Middle East's Leading Boutique Hotel (multiple years)
Condé Nast Traveler Hot List (2015, on opening); first LEED-certified hotel in Oman
items.description: A stone-clad, low-slung Hyatt-luxury retreat woven into the mountainside, Oman's first LEED-certified hotel, all quiet and view.

items.name: The St. Regis Al Mouj Muscat Resort
credentials: Forbes Travel Guide 4-Star (2025)
World Travel Awards, World's Leading New Resort (2025); Oman's Leading Luxury Resort (2025)
items.description: A polished beachfront newcomer beside Muscat's smartest marina-and-golf community, St. Regis butler service and a long private beach.

items.name: Kempinski Hotel Muscat
credentials: Kempinski Hotels, recognised in Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice Awards (2025)
World Travel Awards, Oman's Leading Beach Resort; Business Traveller Middle East, Best Business Hotel in Muscat
items.description: A vast six-kilometre-beachfront European grande-dame resort, eleven dining venues and a private stretch of sand at Al Mouj.

items.name: W Muscat
credentials: Marriott W Hotels (design-forward luxury brand); W Muscat is the brand's Oman debut
Luxury Lifestyle Awards, Luxury Lifestyle Hotel, Oman (2024)
items.description: The brand's beachfront 'W Escape', high-design, high-energy and unabashedly scene-y, right on Shatti Al Qurum.

items.name: Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque
items.description: Oman's grandest mosque and the one unmissable landmark of Muscat, 300,000 tonnes of Indian sandstone, a single hand-woven Persian carpet that took years to make, and a Swarovski chandelier hanging under the main dome. Non-Muslim visitors are welcome between 8 and 11 in the morning (not Fridays); entry is free, dress is modest, and abayas are lent at the gate. Serene and spotless, an easy, moving stop for all generations.

items.name: Royal Opera House Muscat
items.description: The Gulf's leading opera house, Omani stone and marble outside, Islamic, Mughal and European craftsmanship within. Either take a daytime house tour of the auditorium and its inlaid detail, or book an evening of opera, ballet or orchestral music from the October–May season. A refined, dressy night out that families and culture-minded couples both love.

items.name: Mutrah Corniche
items.description: The great curving seafront of old Muscat, whitewashed merchant houses on one side, dhows and the Sultan's harbour on the other, the Hajar hills behind. Walk it late afternoon into golden hour when the light softens and the mosque minarets glow. The gentle, unhurried heart of the city.

items.name: Mutrah Souq
items.description: One of the oldest markets in the Arab world, a warren of covered lanes trading frankincense, silver khanjars, pashminas, antique silver and Omani halwa. Prices are gentle by Dubai standards and the traders are warm, not pushy, good for unhurried, multi-generation browsing. Best late afternoon into the evening when it reopens and comes alive.

items.name: Mutrah Fish Market
items.description: A working morning market under a striking wave-form roof on the harbour, where Omani fishermen land and sell the day's catch. Come at dawn for the full theatre of it, kingfish, tuna and hammour changing hands amid the calls of the auction. Vivid, authentic, and a photographer's delight.

items.name: Al Alam Palace
items.description: The Sultan's ceremonial palace, flamboyant gold-and-blue flared columns framed by manicured avenues, designed by Mumbai's Shapoorji Pallonji firm. You cannot go inside, but the grand approach and the palace flanked by two Portuguese forts is the classic Muscat photograph. A short, easy stop paired with Old Muscat's museums.

items.name: Al Jalali & Al Mirani Forts
items.description: Two 16th-century Portuguese forts guarding the natural harbour on either side of Al Alam Palace. Neither is generally open to the public, but they crown the rocky headlands and give Old Muscat its dramatic, defensible silhouette. Best seen from the palace forecourt or the corniche, especially at dusk.

items.name: National Museum of Oman
items.description: Oman's flagship museum, opposite Al Alam Palace, beautifully lit galleries of the ruling dynasty, Omani silver, frankincense trade, arms and maritime heritage, with Arabic Braille throughout. Cool, calm and well-curated: the single best hour for understanding the country before you explore it. Excellent for curious teenagers.

items.name: Bait Al Zubair Museum
items.description: A private family museum in a cluster of traditional houses, the finest privately held collection of Omani khanjars, jewellery, costume and household life, plus a garden, café and art gallery. Intimate and personal where the National Museum is grand; the two together tell the whole story. On Al Saidiya Street in Old Muscat.

items.name: Ghalya's Museum of Modern Art
items.description: A quiet gem on the Mutrah corniche, a reconstructed Omani house recreating daily life from 1950 to 1975, room by room, with a small modern-art gallery upstairs. Founded by a member of the royal family, it is warm, unhurried and rarely crowded. A tender, human counterpoint to the big state museums.

items.name: Old Muscat walking circuit
items.description: The walled original town behind the corniche, palace, forts, museums, the old Muscat Gate and quiet lanes, all within a compact, walkable radius. A morning here, with a private guide to unlock the history, gives you the founding story of the whole city in a couple of unhurried hours. Shaded stops and easy pacing suit all ages.

items.name: Amouage Perfume Factory & Visitor Centre
items.description: The home of Oman's luxury house of perfume, built on frankincense, myrrh and Omani rose. A complimentary guided tour walks you from raw ingredient to finished bottle, ending in a boutique where you can sample and buy the full collection. A civilised, air-conditioned hour and a genuinely Omani luxury souvenir. Sunday to Thursday, mornings and afternoons.

items.name: Dolphin watching by boat
items.description: Morning boats slip out of the marina to meet wild spinner and common dolphins that ride the bow and leap in their hundreds along this coast. A short, easy two-hour trip, thrilling for children and grandparents alike, with the fort-studded shoreline as backdrop. Best in the calm, cool morning sea.

items.name: Sunset dhow cruise
items.description: Sail the coast at dusk aboard a traditional wooden dhow, past cliffs, coves and the lights of Muscat coming on. Private charters can be arranged with Omani coffee, dates and dinner aboard, a discreet, romantic way to end a day. The gentlest luxury on the water.

items.name: Bandar Khayran
items.description: A hidden labyrinth of turquoise inlets, cliffs and mangroves southeast of the city, 'the blue lagoons', reached by boat or the coast road. Kayak or snorkel the sheltered bays by day, or take a sunset paddle through bioluminescent plankton in winter, when each stroke lights the water. Wild, unspoilt and private-feeling.

items.name: Daymaniyat Islands
items.description: A protected archipelago of nine uninhabited islands about 40km offshore, Oman's finest snorkelling and diving, with clear water, turtles, rays and, in season, whale sharks. Reached by licensed boat with a reserve permit; open roughly October to April. A blue-water day out to rival the Maldives, but a short flight from India. Charter privately for a family.

items.name: Qurum Beach
items.description: A long, clean city beach backed by luxury hotels and the corniche, easy walking, calm swimming and a string of cafés and restaurants. The relaxed everyday beach of Muscat, good for an early stroll or a sunset with the family. Between the Chedi and the Crowne Plaza cliff.

items.name: Qurum Natural Park
items.description: The city's largest green park, lakes, lawns, shaded walks, playgrounds and a rose garden set behind the beach. A cool, family-friendly escape for an evening, popular with local families. Simple, safe and easy with young children or grandparents.

items.name: Afternoon tea at The Chedi Muscat
items.description: Oman's most stylish resort, long reflecting pools, minimalist Omani-Zen design and a serene Lobby Lounge that serves an exquisite afternoon tea. Even non-residents can book in for tea or dinner and soak up the calm. Discreet luxury of exactly the kind that beats Dubai's glitz. Vegetarian and dietary requests handled with ease.

items.name: Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
items.description: A landmark hotel set between mountains and a private bay, with a soaring 38-metre domed atrium lobby. Come for afternoon tea beneath the dome or a beachfront dinner even if you stay elsewhere, one of Muscat's grand, gracious dining experiences. The setting alone is worth the drive.

items.name: Nizwa Fort & Souq
items.description: The old imamate capital, 90 minutes inland, a massive 17th-century round-towered fort you can climb for sweeping views, beside a restored souq trading silver, dates, pottery and frankincense. The cultural heart of Oman's interior, and an easy, rewarding day trip with a private car. Best paired with the Friday goat market.

items.name: Nizwa Friday Goat Market
items.description: Every Friday from around 6am, traders parade goats and cattle in a shouting, bargaining ring beside Nizwa Souq while deals are sealed over Omani coffee. Raw, theatrical and utterly authentic, a slice of living Oman found nowhere in Dubai. Come early; it is over by mid-morning.

items.name: Jabreen Castle
items.description: The most beautiful of Oman's castles, a 1670 palace-fort with painted wooden ceilings, hidden chambers, date-store rooms and a canal running through it. Small, intimate and gorgeously preserved, it rewards a slow wander. An easy pairing with Bahla Fort just up the road.

items.name: Bahla Fort
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Bahla Fort
items.description: Oman's only UNESCO-listed fort, a vast 13th-century mud-brick citadel with a 12km oasis wall, steeped in local legend. Recently restored, it is monumental and atmospheric, the great fortress of the interior. Combine with neighbouring Jabreen Castle and Nizwa for a full interior day.

items.name: Jebel Akhdar rose terraces
items.area: Al Jabal Al Akhdar (day trip / overnight)
items.description: The 'Green Mountain', stepped villages clinging to slopes above 2,000m where Damask roses bloom each March–April and are distilled into Oman's famous rosewater. Walk the terraced village trail, visit an old distillery, and stay high at Alila or Anantara for cool air and canyon-edge infinity pools. Cooler, greener and utterly different from the coast.

items.name: Alila Jabal Akhdar
items.description: A serene stone-built retreat perched on the mountain plateau, all clean lines, big views and a spa above the clouds. The mountain base of choice for couples and families wanting quiet luxury, mountain walks and cool nights. Stay a night to feel Oman's other, alpine self.

items.name: Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar
items.description: The highest five-star resort in the Middle East, on the very lip of a canyon with a dramatic cliff-edge pool and rose-ritual spa. Refined, warm and spectacular, guided rose-farm and mountain-guru walks included. A destination in its own right for a multi-generation stay.

items.name: Jebel Shams, the Balcony Walk
items.description: Oman's highest peak overlooks Wadi Ghul, a 1,000m-deep gorge known as the Grand Canyon of Arabia. The Balcony Walk hugs the rim to an abandoned village, with a rustic canyon-edge café just minutes along for those who want only the view. Cool clear air and vast panoramas; go October to April. Best with a guide and a 4x4.

items.name: Wahiba Sands (Sharqiya Sands)
items.description: A sea of amber dunes over 100m tall, home to the Bedu. Ride the crests by 4x4, meet a Bedouin family, then sleep in a luxury desert camp under a spread of stars with dinner over the fire. The classic Arabian desert night, thrilling for children, magical for all. Book a tented camp with private, comfortable suites.

items.name: Wadi Bani Khalid
items.description: The most accessible of Oman's great wadis, emerald spring-fed pools among palms and smooth boulders, a five-minute walk from the car park, with a café overlooking the water. Swim in the warm rock pools or stroll the gorge; there is even a cave for the adventurous. Family-easy and gorgeous. Pairs with a Wahiba desert night.

items.name: Wadi Shab
items.description: Oman's most celebrated wadi hike, a short boat across the mouth, then an easy trail past turquoise pools to a hidden cave waterfall you swim to reach. About two hours from Muscat and doable in a day. Bring water shoes; the reward at the end is unforgettable. Best for active families and couples.

items.name: Bimmah Sinkhole
items.description: A turquoise limestone sinkhole, 20m deep and fed by mixed sea and fresh water, that locals call the 'falling star'. Steps lead down to a swim, and tiny fish nibble your feet. A quick, delightful stop on the coastal road to Wadi Shab or Sur, easy for everyone.

items.name: Wadi Tiwi
items.description: The 'Wadi of Nine Villages', a narrower, greener gorge than neighbouring Wadi Shab, with terraced plantations, falaj channels and turquoise pools between towering walls. Quieter and lush, best explored by 4x4 and on foot. A serene pairing with Wadi Shab on the Sur road.

items.name: Ras Al Jinz Turtle Reserve
items.description: One of the Indian Ocean's most important green-turtle nesting beaches, where thousands return each year. On a ranger-led night or dawn walk you watch a female haul ashore, dig and lay by moonlight, a hushed, once-in-a-lifetime moment. Stay at the reserve's eco-lodge to be first on the beach. Peak nesting summer, but turtles come year-round.

items.name: Sur, dhow shipyard & Ayjah
items.description: A coastal town two hours south where master craftsmen still build wooden dhows by eye, without plans. Watch the shipwrights, cross to the whitewashed fishing village of Ayjah and its Portuguese-era lighthouse over the lagoon. A living slice of Oman's great seafaring past. Good base for Ras Al Jinz.

items.name: Al Hamra & Bait Al Safah
items.description: One of Oman's best-preserved old towns, with three-century-old mud-brick houses stacked below the Hajar. At Bait Al Safah, a 400-year-old house turned living museum, local women grind coffee, bake bread and press oil the old way. Warm, hands-on heritage the whole family enjoys. Combine with Misfat and Jebel Shams.

items.name: Misfat al Abriyeen
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Aflaj Irrigation Systems of Oman
items.description: A tumbling mountain village of mud-brick homes and shaded date terraces fed by ancient falaj channels, 1,000m up. Wander the lanes and green plantations, or stay in a restored guesthouse to feel the quiet. One of Oman's most photogenic villages, and gloriously unspoilt. Reached on the Al Hamra road.

items.name: Nakhal Fort & A'Thowarah Hot Springs
items.description: A dramatic fort built onto a rock outcrop above date plantations and the Hajar foothills, impossible to photograph badly, with warm mineral springs running through palm groves a short drive on. A gentle, scenic half-day loop from Muscat. Easy and rewarding for all ages.

items.name: Rustaq Fort
items.description: One of Oman's largest forts in a former capital, with towering walls, a mosque and its own hot spring within. Less visited than Nizwa, so often quiet, and paired naturally with Nakhal on the Batinah loop. A grand, uncrowded fort day for history-lovers.

items.name: Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
credentials: UNESCO World Heritage Site, Archaeological Sites of Bat, Al-Khutm and Al-Ayn
items.description: A 5,000-year-old Bronze Age necropolis of stone beehive tombs and towers near Ibri, the most complete such ensemble in Arabia, from the age when Omani copper reached Mesopotamia. Remote, atmospheric and rarely crowded; a private guide brings the ancient trade world alive. For travellers who want the deep past. Combine with Bahla.

items.name: Jebel Sifah
items.description: A resort marina town on the coast south of Muscat, ringed by mountains and a long sandy beach with calm swimming and a golf course. An easy, laid-back seaside escape, kayaking, boat trips and quiet sand within an hour of the city. Good for a relaxed family day by the water.

items.name: Yiti Beach
items.description: A wild, quiet cove reached over the coastal hills from Muscat, with a hidden stretch that feels like a private beach. Big skies, few people and mountains meeting the sea, a favourite for a peaceful picnic or sunset drive. Best with a 4x4 and no fixed plans.

items.name: Wadi Al Arbeieen
items.description: A dramatic mountain wadi of blue-green pools among palms, less trodden than the famous names, about 1hr45 from the city. The scenic mountain drive in is half the pleasure; the pools reward those who make the effort. A 4x4 and a guide are recommended, a proper off-the-map day.

items.name: Muscat Gate & city viewpoints
items.description: The old ceremonial gate marking the entrance to Old Muscat, near the giant Riyam incense-burner monument on its hill. Climb for a panorama over the corniche, harbour and forts, a quick, free stop that frames the whole old city. Lovely near sunset.

items.name: Private guide & 4x4 grand tour
items.description: The best way to see Oman: a licensed private driver-guide and a comfortable 4x4 to link the forts, wadis, mountains and desert at your own pace, with the history unlocked and the logistics handled. Dietary needs, including Jain and pure-vegetarian, are easily arranged ahead. Discreet, flexible and ideal for a multi-generation family.

items.name: The Beach Restaurant, The Chedi Muscat
items.area: The Chedi Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
credentials: Within The Chedi Muscat (Forbes 4-Star; World Travel Awards World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa)
items.description: Sand-underfoot seafood by the Gulf, Iranian and Caspian caviar, freshly shucked oysters and the line-caught catch of the day.

items.name: Diana's Point, Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar
items.area: Jebal Akhdar (Green Mountain), ~2hr drive from Muscat
credentials: Within Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar (Condé Nast Traveler Gold List; World Travel Awards Oman's Leading Luxury Resort)
items.description: Private canyon-edge dining on the promontory where Princess Diana once stood, the most dramatic table in the country.

items.name: The Restaurant, The Chedi Muscat
items.area: The Chedi Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
credentials: Within The Chedi Muscat (Forbes 4-Star; World Travel Awards World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa)
items.description: Four open kitchens, Arabic, Indian, Asian and Mediterranean, under one high, chandeliered ceiling; the Chedi's flagship all-day room.

items.name: Al Angham
items.area: Royal Opera House Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
credentials: Set within the Royal Opera House Muscat cultural complex, Oman's flagship dedicated fine-dining Omani restaurant
items.description: The finest room dedicated to Omani cuisine, carved-plaster grandeur beside the Opera House, serving the sultanate's own dishes with real ceremony.

items.name: Bukhara, Kempinski Hotel Muscat
credentials: Within Kempinski Hotel Muscat (Condé Nast Traveller Readers' Choice 2025; World Travel Awards Oman's Leading Beach Resort)
items.description: Robust North Indian cooking from the clay tandoor, inside the city's largest beach resort, familiar flavours, done with polish.

items.name: Shahi Darbar (fine Indian dining)
credentials: Established Muscat Indian restaurant with a consistent local reputation
items.description: Long-standing, well-regarded North Indian kitchen with a devoted local following, generous, familiar, unfussy.

items.name: Ubhar
items.area: Bareeq Al Shatti, Shatti Al Qurum
credentials: Widely cited (Time Out Muscat and others) as Muscat's leading modern Omani restaurant
items.description: Modern Omani-and-Arabian cooking that treats the sultanate's home dishes seriously, shuwa, harees, camel, done with pride.

items.name: Kargeen Café
credentials: An enduring Muscat institution, widely recommended for atmosphere and authentic mezze
items.description: Lantern-lit garden courtyards and generous Omani-Levantine mezze, the city's most-loved relaxed table, buzzing past midnight.

items.name: Bin Ateeq
credentials: Long-established local institution for authentic traditional Omani cuisine
items.description: Floor-seated, private-room dining on Omani classics, shuwa and majboos served the old way, with no ceremony and real honesty.

items.name: The bar at Al Husn, a Waldorf Astoria Hotel
credentials: Within Al Husn, a Waldorf Astoria Hotel (Barr Al Jissah landmark; former Forbes 4-Star Shangri-La Al Husn)
items.description: Clifftop sundowners above a private cove at the crown of the Barr Al Jissah headland, the classic Muscat sunset drink, now under the Waldorf Astoria flag.

items.name: Duke's Bar, Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel
credentials: Within Al Bustan Palace, a Ritz-Carlton Hotel (Forbes Recommended; World Travel Awards World's Leading Palace Hotel)
items.description: A classic hotel bar beneath the palace's soaring atrium, the grande-dame address for a measured evening drink in Muscat.

items.name: The Long Bar, The Chedi Muscat
items.area: The Chedi Muscat, Shatti Al Qurum
credentials: Within The Chedi Muscat (Forbes 4-Star; World Travel Awards World's Leading Luxury Beach Resort & Spa)
items.description: A hushed, low-lit lounge inside Oman's design icon, considered cocktails and a fireside calm, the most refined drink in the city.

items.name: Al Burj cocktail bar, Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar
items.area: Jebal Akhdar (Green Mountain), ~2hr drive from Muscat
credentials: Within Anantara Al Jabal Al Akhdar (Condé Nast Traveler Gold List; World Travel Awards Oman's Leading Luxury Resort)
items.description: A Moroccan-style bar set in the tower of the resort's fort, cocktails 2,000m up with the canyon falling away below, a drink you don't forget.

plan.heading: 3 days in Muscat, done well
plan.lede: A day-by-day shape for the trip, the pace we would set. Your advisor books the flights and the rooms; the days are yours.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: The Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque at opening, its single carpet and chandelier, then the Royal Opera House exterior.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Check into the Chedi Muscat, lunch by the long pool, then an afternoon in Muttrah Souq and along the corniche.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner at The Restaurant at the Chedi, then the sea from the beach terrace.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: Drive into the Hajar mountains to Nizwa's round fort and the Friday livestock market.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Lunch at the Alila Jabal Akhdar on the canyon rim, then the terraced rose villages of Saiq.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: Dinner on the escarpment as the light drops into Wadi Ghul.

slots.label: Morning
slots.text: A morning at Wadi Shab, walking to the hidden pool and swimming where few reach.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.text: Drive the coast to Bimmah, then a late lunch of fresh hammour by the water.

slots.label: Evening
slots.text: A quiet last dinner back at the Chedi, and mint tea under the frankincense trees.

items.name: Mutrah
items.description: For the old corniche and the atmospheric souk, the most characterful place to walk at dusk.

items.name: Shatti Al Qurum
items.description: For beachfront hotels and easy dining, close to the museums and the city's centre of gravity.

items.name: Al Mouj
items.description: For a marina base with a golf course and newer restaurants, quieter and a little removed.

events.name: Muscat Festival
events.note: A month of crafts, culture and food across the city's parks during the cool season.

events.name: Salalah Khareef
events.note: In Oman's far south, the monsoon turns the hills green, a summer escape unlike anywhere else in Arabia.

onGround.heading: On the ground
onGround.note: Oman is quietly conservative and exceptionally courteous; dress modestly, cover shoulders and knees, and women should carry a scarf for the Sultan Qaboos Grand Mosque. The Chedi and the Al Bustan Palace are the reference addresses; pair the city with a night in the Hajar mountains or the Wahiba Sands.

rows.label: Arriving
rows.value: Fly into Muscat International (MCT), a calm modern airport, where a meet-and-assist and a chauffeured car take you along the coast to Shatti Al Qurum or the Al Mouj marina.

rows.label: Getting around
rows.value: A private driver is essential, the sights spread along the coast and into the mountains, and Muttrah's corniche and souq are made for an unhurried evening walk.

rows.label: Connectivity
rows.value: An eSIM from Omantel or Ooredoo covers the city and main roads on 4G/5G; signal thins in the interior wadis and dunes, so download maps ahead.

rows.label: Money
rows.value: The Omani rial (OMR) is one of the world's highest-valued currencies; cards work in hotels and cities, but keep cash for souqs and rural stops, and tipping is modest and welcomed.

rows.label: Climate
rows.value: November to March is the sweet spot: pleasant 20-30C days for the coast, forts and wadis. Avoid May-September, when heat climbs to 38-40C and travel becomes exhausting; June is the peak of it.

rows.label: Flights from India
rows.value: Direct from Delhi (about 3.5 hours) and Mumbai (about 2h 45m, the shortest hop), also from Bengaluru. Oman Air flies it best in business, an understated and gracious product. Muscat's compact airport makes it an easy, calm arrival with none of the mega-hub scramble.

rows.label: Health & safety
rows.value: No special vaccinations; routine plus hepatitis A and typhoid is prudent. Oman is exceptionally safe and among the most courteous countries in the region. Tap water is treated and considered safe, though bottled is widely preferred. Heat, not crime, is the risk.

rows.label: Dining, veg & Jain
rows.value: Comfortable for vegetarian and Jain travellers. A large Indian community means Indian food is genuinely good and everywhere; pure-veg is well understood. Gujarati and South Indian kitchens across Ruwi and Al Khuwair are reliable, and resort hotels prepare Jain on request.
